subject: No-train controls, prompt/response ownership & escrow options for NovaHealth pilot
messages:
From: Caroline Young <caroline.young@novahealth.ai>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: legalops@novahealth.ai
Date: 2026-07-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot — no-train guarantee & escrow options

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking a look at NovaHealth's pilot request. We're evaluating Redwood for a 6-week clinical triage pilot and need clarity on a few points before procurement will greenlight the PO. High-level asks:

- A contractual no-training commitment for any prompts/responses generated during the pilot (we need the data excluded from model improvement and internal benchmarking).
- Confirmation of prompt/response ownership: NovaHealth must retain exclusive rights to outputs produced from our tenant during the pilot.
- Practical evidence we can present to security: how no-train is enforced (ops/architecture), a scrubbed snapshot of logs or an escrow mechanism we could use for audits.

I've attached our DPA questions (NovaHealth-DPA-questions.pdf) — the legal team flagged the escrow idea as a fallback if you can't provide technical isolation immediately. Procurement is aiming for a mid-August start; can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to these controls for a pilot? If so, what artifacts / timeline do you need from us?

Thanks,
Caroline Young
Head of Platform Security | NovaHealth
caroline.young@novahealth.ai

Subject: Re: Pilot — no-train guarantee & escrow options

Caroline —

Appreciate the clear ask and the DPA doc. Short answer: we can support a no-training contractual commitment and demonstrable operational controls for a pilot, but the implementation varies by deployment mode.

Summary of options we typically offer:

1) Dedicated tenant (recommended for pilots):
- Contractually bind Redwood not to use pilot data for model training or benchmarking.
- Tenant-level toggle that disables retention to training lakes; logs remain available for debug but are excluded from improvement pipelines.
- Evidence bundle: architecture diagram, ops runbook, SOC 2 control mapping, and a one-off redacted log export for compliance review.

2) Private deployment (VPC/on-prem):
- Full isolation — no inbound data leaves customer environment unless explicitly configured. We can provide attestation and on-prem validation.

3) Hosted customers without a dedicated tenant:
- We offer contractual language to prevent training on customer data, but operational separation (no shared tenant) is stronger.

For the pilot timeline and artifacts:
- I attached a DPA redline we typically start from (redwood-dpa-draft.docx) and our evidence checklist (no-train-evidence-checklist.xlsx).
- Next steps: 30-minute call this week with Caroline + LegalOps + our security/product engineering (I can invite Dev Patel and Marcus Lin to cover ops and dataflow).

I'll summarize the operational controls on the call and follow up with the runbook and a redacted log sample. If NovaHealth prefers an escrow of transformed logs, we can discuss accepted formats and retention windows.

Best,

Hi Caroline — quick technical note from the infra side to complement Irene's email.

How we implement no-training for a dedicated pilot tenant (practical details):
- Tenant isolation: a unique tenant id is provisioned; ingestion pipelines are tagged and routed to an isolated storage namespace.
- Training exclusion: a config flip disables downstream jobs from consuming that namespace; this is enforced by our orchestration layer and audited in our job scheduler.
- KV cache and ephemeral state: per-session KV caches live only for the user session and are purged after configured TTLs. We can shorten TTLs for the pilot.
- Logging and telemetry: we can provide a redacted, timestamped audit log that shows request/response hashes and delivery metadata (no PII).
- Subprocessors: our inference runtime and S3-like storage are subprocessors; we can offer onshore storage and KMS key scoping for the pilot.

Evidence we can produce within a week of engagement:
- No-train ops runbook (attached: no-train-ops-runbook.pdf)
- Redacted log export (CSV) with hashing and sampling rules
- Short architecture diagram showing dataflow and exclusion points

Limitations / notes:
- For hosted shared-tenants we can't retroactively exclude data from past ingestion; exclusion must be enabled at tenant provision time.
- Model weights escrow is atypical; most customers want a log-level escrow for compliance rather than model source. If NovaHealth needs escrowed artifacts, we can accept a redacted log deposit to a mutually agreed SFTP or escrow provider.

Happy to walk through these on a screen-share — Irene, proposing a 30-min slot tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PT.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Irene and Dev — this is helpful. A couple follow-ups from Legal and Procurement: 

1) Prompt/response ownership: Legal wants explicit language that NovaHealth owns outputs generated by our tenant during the pilot and that Redwood will not assert derivatives or model rights over those outputs. Can you confirm Redwood will accept that in a pilot DPA/addendum?

2) Escrow: Procurement prefers a redacted-log escrow to model-weight escrow. We need to understand the format and whether Redwood will deposit a nightly redacted bundle to an SFTP we control (or to an escrow provider). If you can outline a sample retention/transfer process we can take that to our procurement counsel.

3) Timeline/budget: Procurement has a cost-neutral constraint for pilot approvals; if dedicated tenant provisioning has a setup fee, please flag it now so we can build the PO.

Would be great to include someone from Oxford Legal (our outside counsel) on the call if possible — copying LegalOps. We're good for the proposed time tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PT.

--
Caroline

Caroline — thanks, quick confirmations and next steps below.

1) Ownership & derivative rights: Redwood will accept pilot-level language that assigns outputs produced by NovaHealth's tenant to NovaHealth and prevents Redwood from asserting derivative/model improvement rights on pilot data. We'll include a short addendum to the DPA with clear scope (pilot tenant + dates).

2) Escrow/log deposit: We can support nightly redacted log exports to an SFTP or escrow provider. Typical format: compressed CSV (request_id, request_hash, response_hash, timestamp, redaction_version) plus a signed manifest. We will also provide hashing and sampling rules so NovaHealth can validate completeness. We will not deposit model weights.

3) Costs and provisioning: a one-time setup fee for a dedicated pilot tenant is standard for pilots that require tenant-level isolation and onshore KMS scoping. I'll have finance prepare an itemized quote; if procurement needs a cost-neutral arrangement we can discuss a credit-backed short-term waiver for POC customers.

Attachments included in this thread for your review: redwood-dpa-draft.docx, no-train-evidence-checklist.xlsx, no-train-ops-runbook.pdf

Meeting: Scheduled for 2026-07-23 10:00 PT (we'll keep it, and I'll add Marcus for a short ops walkthrough). I'll also include a DocuSign link for the DPA addendum after the call: https://docusign.com/redsigned/NH-4521
